grades.quote: To tell the hardware and compiler not to re-order, xv6 uses __sync_synchronize() in both acquire (1271) and release (1302). __sync_synchronize() is a _memory barrier_ : it tells the compiler and CPU to not reorder loads or stores across the barrier.
grades.reason: Directly explains why lock acquisition and release use barriers to order shared-memory accesses.
Discusses condition-variable synchronization, not memory ordering or barriers for atomic locks.

grades.quote: To help implement multiprocessor synchronization, the AMOs optionally provide release consistency semantics. If the _aq_ bit is set, then no later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the AMO. Conversely, if the _rl_ bit is set, then other RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding the AMO in this RISC-V hart.
grades.reason: Explains that atomic operations need ordering semantics, supplied through aq/rl bits or the fences discussed later, and demonstrates their use in a spinlock.

grades.quote: Both types of atomic instruction support various memory consistency orderings including unordered, acquire, release, and sequentially consistent semantics.
grades.reason: Usefully distinguishes atomicity from ordering, but does not explain barrier requirements for critical sections.
